nodes.label: Bare onClick reference never resolves in reachesPlayAudio
nodes.rationale: Reused id: same claim, same mechanism. This note reaches it independently while classifying its own queue — 'The detector resolves named references only for `raisesToast`, not for `reachesPlayAudio`. This is a systematic detector bug affecting many chunks (any `onClick={handler}` where handler cues)' — which is the same defect chunk-rem-008 recorded at the plan level.
nodes.norm_label: bare on click reference never resolves in reaches play audio

nodes.label: indexFunctions regex cannot index typed parameter lists
nodes.rationale: Reused id: same mechanism. Here it is worked out for one concrete declaration — `const run = async (kind: string, fn: () => Promise<void>) => {`, whose inner `)` ends the regex's `\([^)]*\)` param match before `=> {`, so `run` is never indexed and the button that calls it is reported silent.
nodes.norm_label: index functions regex cannot index typed parameter lists

nodes.label: A doc comment containing a literal onClick={ example becomes a phantom detector candidate
nodes.rationale: Reused id: same claim. This note paid the cost — its own explanatory comment at line 600 spelled out `onClick={handleToggleRich}`, the detector's `\bonClick\s*=\s*\{` matched inside the comment, and the line surfaced as an unaccounted key that had to be diagnosed as a comment before the wording could be trimmed.
nodes.norm_label: a doc comment containing a literal on click example becomes a phantom detector candidate

nodes.label: stopPropagation backdrop shield is not a control
nodes.rationale: Reused id: same claim, applied to ConfirmDialog.tsx:97. The panel's onClick exists only to stop the backdrop's dismiss path, so 'cueing it would report a dismissal that never happens; the backdrop (ConfirmDialog.tsx:82) is the only dismiss path that sounds'.
nodes.norm_label: stop propagation backdrop shield is not a control

nodes.label: Cross-module prop handler cues in the parent component
nodes.rationale: Reused id: same claim, here proved by reading the single call site. `onCancel={handleCancelDelete}` calls `playAudio("close_001.ogg")` and `onConfirm={() => void handleConfirmDelete()}` plays `trash_001.ogg`, so both ConfirmDialog buttons already cue at the call site and a cue inside the primitive would double-fire.
nodes.norm_label: cross module prop handler cues in the parent component

nodes.label: Fixing the detector to resolve bare references makes every self-sounding exclusion stale
nodes.rationale: The parent rewrote the detector to resolve bare references and added EXEMPT_FROM_REVERIFICATION at the same time, because a 'no exclusion is stale' test requires every exclusion key to still be in detectedKeys. A control that was a false positive precisely because its handler was invisible stops being detected the moment the handler is followed, so the record that documented the old blind spot is invalidated by the fix for it.
nodes.norm_label: fixing the detector to resolve bare references makes every self sounding exclusion stale

nodes.label: The parent rewrote and then reverted the shared contract file while nine agents were writing to it
nodes.rationale: A different mechanism from the git-checkout and git-stash clobbers already recorded: audioCueCoverage.test.ts was observed at 572 lines, then 826 with the detector fixed, then back at 572 lines byte-identical to the original, then 704. Every append this chunk made was lost at least once and had to be re-applied, and the KNOWN_GAPS queue came back holding the 11 original entries.
nodes.norm_label: the parent rewrote and then reverted the shared contract file while nine agents were writing to it

nodes.label: self-sounding was extended by concurrent chunks to mean the handler already cues, not that the element plays the cue under test
nodes.rationale: Two sibling chunks had already settled on the reading before this chunk did: 'self-sounding = the handler already plays a cue, so a call-site cue would double-fire', extending the original sense from AudioSettingsSection:336. Having made its opposite choice first — editing production source to make the detector legible — this chunk reverted those edits to match, on the grounds that a register entry is a permanent blind spot once written and the detector is the thing that should be fixed.
nodes.norm_label: self sounding was extended by concurrent chunks to mean the handler already cues not that the element plays the cue under test

nodes.label: The exclusion register's justification test accepts four classes while the manifest lists five, so deliberate-prior-decision cannot be used as a reason
nodes.rationale: The brief's rule 6 offers `shared-primitive`|`toast-owns-cue`|`self-sounding`|`high-frequency`|`deliberate-prior-decision`, but the enforcing test's regex is only `/shared-primitive|self-sounding|high-frequency|toast-owns-cue/`. A reason naming only deliberate-prior-decision therefore fails with 'an exclusion lost its justification', which forces the prior decision into the prose while the class word is chosen from the four that pass.
nodes.norm_label: the exclusion register's justification test accepts four classes while the manifest lists five so deliberate prior decision cannot be used as a reason

nodes.label: The import trigger's cue belongs at the file-pick, not at the button press, because the keyboard shortcut shares the same downstream chain
nodes.rationale: Both the header button and useNoteEditorShortcuts' onRequestImportTrigger funnel into `importInputRef.current?.click()`, and the single existing cue is in handleImportFileSelect when a file is actually chosen. Cueing only the button would give two sounds per successful import and leave the shortcut path silent, so the DRY place is the input's change handler and the trigger stays silent.
nodes.norm_label: the import trigger's cue belongs at the file pick not at the button press because the keyboard shortcut shares the same downstream chain

nodes.label: ConfirmDialog's backdrop dismissal already plays two close cues, one in the primitive and one in the caller
nodes.rationale: A pre-existing double cue found while auditing and deliberately not fixed: the backdrop handler plays CLOSE at ConfirmDialog.tsx:82 and then calls onCancel, whose caller handleCancelDelete plays close_001.ogg again. Introduced by commit 609561596; the fix belongs in NotesWorkspace.tsx, which was outside the owned file list.
nodes.norm_label: confirm dialog's backdrop dismissal already plays two close cues one in the primitive and one in the caller

nodes.label: SWITCH was chosen for the rich/plain mode toggle on the reviewed NotesSidebar precedent, not from the brief's three-cue list
nodes.rationale: The brief names CLICK, SELECT and SUCCESS/ERROR as the cues that recur, which reads as a closed list; the catalog and the reviewed reference file are wider. NotesSidebar, the file the brief names as the established pattern, already uses SOUND_EFFECTS.SWITCH for a boolean toggle and SELECT for filter pills, and 609561596 used OPEN, CLOSE, CONFIRMATION, TRASH, PLUCK and TICK_FORMAT.
nodes.norm_label: switch was chosen for the rich plain mode toggle on the reviewed note sidebar precedent not from the brief's three cue list

nodes.label: The rich/plain toggle button cues but its keyboard shortcut stays silent, because the shared hook was outside the owned file list
nodes.rationale: useNoteEditorShortcuts reaches the toggle through useRichTextToggle, which has no sound. The cue was placed in the handler the queued button calls, which leaves the shortcut path silent — an asymmetry knowingly introduced because the DRY place, useRichTextToggle.ts, was not in the chunk's file list and taking a file outside the list was a STOP.
nodes.norm_label: the rich plain toggle button cues but its keyboard shortcut stays silent because the shared hook was outside the owned file list

nodes.label: A new column is declared in CREATE TABLE and in the guarded ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN migration list, so pre-existing databases open unchanged
nodes.rationale: The has_col guard makes the migration idempotent in both directions: a fresh database already carries the column so the ALTER is a no-op, and an existing database gets it with SQLite's ADD COLUMN default backfilling every row to 0. The brief states the constraint the design answers — 'old DBs must open unchanged'.
nodes.norm_label: a new column is declared in create table and in the guarded alter table add column migration list so pre existing databases open unchanged

nodes.label: is_safe_sql_type already permits INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, so a NOT NULL additive column needs no allow-list change
nodes.rationale: The migration runner type-checks every column definition against an allow-list before it will run the ALTER. Checking the list first showed '"INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0" is already in is_safe_sql_type', which is why the proposed group_cols entry needed no accompanying change to the guard.
nodes.norm_label: is safe sql type already permits integer not null default zero so a not null additive column needs no allow list change

nodes.label: is_group_tagged_for_research returns Ok(false) for both an unknown uuid and a missing column, so the analytics ledger path never errors
nodes.rationale: Two failure classes are folded into Ok(false) rather than Err: QueryReturnedNoRows for a uuid that is not a group, and a 'no such column' message from a database opened without its migrations. The stated reason is that 'the analytics ledger path never errors' and ledger writes stay metadata-only and total.
nodes.norm_label: is group tagged for research returns ok false for both an unknown uuid and a missing column so the analytics ledger path never errors

nodes.label: research_mode_enabled is a preferences-table key written through the existing set_preference, defaulting false where the embedding prefs idiom defaults true
nodes.rationale: No new setter is introduced: the write path reuses preferences::set_preference(key, "true"/"false"). The read mirrors services/embedding_prefs.rs's KEY_ string-"true" idiom but inverts its default — `unwrap_or(false)`, unlike embedding prefs which default true — because this toggle gates analytics rather than enabling them.
nodes.norm_label: research mode enabled is a preferences table key written through the existing set preference defaulting false where the embedding prefs idiom defaults true

nodes.label: A NULL group_id on a snippet short-circuits to Ok(false) at the call site instead of issuing a NULL = ? comparison
nodes.rationale: The caller passes an Option and None returns early, so the query never runs. The note states the reason directly: 'never queries (no `NULL = ?` trap)' — SQL three-valued logic would make the comparison never true and silently drop the row instead of returning untagged.
nodes.norm_label: a null group id on a snippet short circuits to ok false at the call site instead of issuing a null comparison
